amendments.reason: review MAJOR: the criterion claimed every harness artefact is hidden while the test asserted a self-chosen 4-item list; a fresh repo seeded with the template still shows 7 untracked runtime paths that this repo's own root ignore already covers — the same omission class as the previous round's CRITICAL
amendments.superseded_statement: when the seeded ignore file is in place and the harness writes its artefacts, then `git status --porcelain` reports nothing.
amendments.statement: when a fresh project is seeded with the shipped ignore template and every path the runtime actually writes is created, then git reports nothing dirty — the paths come from the writers in the code, not from a list the test chose for itself

amendments.reason: review MINOR: labelling dirty-tree whenever status is non-empty sends the operator to clean the tree when the actual obstacle is a diverged base that no cleaning will fix
amendments.superseded_statement: when git refuses the fast-forward, then the report names `dirty-tree` if the tree was dirty and `non-ff-or-no-remote` if it was clean.
amendments.statement: when git refuses the fast-forward, then the report separates a genuine divergence from a merely dirty tree, so the operator is pointed at the real obstacle

additions.reason: review CRITICAL: base_advanced reads updated==true, which the others/fetch path sets false for a base that CONTAINS origin's tip — the authorising fact is true and the gate reads false, stranding the unit forever with the inverted label base-behind
additions.statement: when the unit's base already HOLDS origin's tip (it is ahead of origin, so the fetch refuses), then the prune is authorised — the gate reads the fact, not the fetch exit status

additions.reason: review CRITICAL: the carve-out allows the write but the ignore landed only in the template, and seed_gitignore preserves an existing file — so no already-initialised project, this one included, ever receives it
additions.statement: when the write gate allows a scratch path in this repository, then git also ignores it, so an add -A cannot sweep throwaway evidence into the unit

additions.reason: review CRITICAL, second half: seed_gitignore preserves an existing file, so a template line added today never reaches any project initialised yesterday — which is why the scratch carve-out shipped without its safety net
additions.statement: when the harness seeds its ignore file over one that already exists, then the lines missing from it are appended instead of the whole file being skipped, so an already-initialised project receives new entries

additions.reason: review MAJOR raised independently by both reviewers: restoredToUnit runs a real git checkout on the refusal path and is published in the report, with no test and no criterion naming it
additions.statement: when the prune is refused on an in-place unit, then the checkout is restored to the unit branch and the report says so, so the refusal leaves the operator where the work is
